notes: Every requirement maps to executable checks. A check that cannot run is BLOCKED, never PASS. severity=release blocks the gate; severity=tracked is reported and listed as an unresolved risk.

requirements.title: A business category selects its own room; an unknown key cannot escape to an arbitrary room
requirements.why: Room selection is the product's core promise: the workspace is built from the business.

checks.title: every kind the schema allows has a room
the same spec always opens the same room
an unknown kind cannot escape to an arbitrary room
different businesses get different environments, not one template

requirements.title: SceneSpec is zod-validated: coordinates/colours, duplicate ids and out-of-bounds panels are rejected
requirements.why: The model decides WHAT, never coordinates. A permissive schema lets a hostile reply draw the product.

checks.title: spec: a coordinate or colour anywhere is rejected, not dropped
spec: duplicate ids are a failure
spec: panel count bounds are enforced

requirements.title: Model failure modes (empty, malformed, timeout, error) fall back to a valid spec instead of failing
requirements.why: A provider outage must degrade the workspace, not break it.

checks.title: compose: no model configured falls back instead of failing
compose: non-JSON, bad schema and model failure all fall back
compose: a model timeout falls back within the budget
compose: a valid model answer is used as-is

requirements.title: Model-generated room selection verified against a real provider
requirements.why: Compose tests use a fake provider. Without credentials the product's live path is unproven.

checks.justification: No provider key is present in .env and Pollinations answers 402. Every accepted proof so far is the fallback path. This is reported as an unresolved risk, not a pass.

requirements.title: Scene contracts hold: deterministic procedural set, dptscn parses, corrupt magic rejected
requirements.why: The backdrop is generated code; a silent non-determinism breaks every visual gate downstream.

checks.title: procedural set: every room produces a deterministic cloud in metres
dptscn: every built scene parses with consistent lengths
dptscn: a corrupt magic is rejected, not half-parsed

requirements.title: Engineering provenance never reaches the product surface
requirements.why: Roadmap words on screen are a product leak, and were fixed once already.

checks.title: the welcome heading collapses to zero tracking only under RTL or Persian

requirements.title: Authorization boundaries and data isolation hold on the server
requirements.why: The office serves more than one business; a leak between them is a trust failure.

requirements.title: A production build produces both artifacts, freshly, from this commit
requirements.why: The gate runs the build script declared in the judged commit, then hashes both artifacts and requires them to be newer than this run.

requirements.title: Look-lock art gates pass on frames rendered from this commit
requirements.why: The look is the product. A green unit suite says nothing about it.

requirements.title: Responsive layout: no overflow, no text overlap, no under-size fonts or touch targets
requirements.why: The office is used on phones; layout failures are invisible to unit tests.

requirements.title: The release records check passes at the commit under judgement
requirements.why: verify/release-check.mjs is a step the gate runs. While no requirement named it, its exit code was printed in the step line and ignored by the verdict, so a broken release record could ship behind a PASS.
